name: Standing By
tagline: You've seen them at their worst. You're still here.
epigraph: Mark Twain wrote home for four things to be waiting. Three are in this glass.
glassware: small wine glass, chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v3, confirmed r6): swap test against the Nurse, Rescuer, Healer, Reassurer, Doctor, Craftsman and Researcher passes; no partner required, no gender about the guest. Pronouns in yours 1–4 are Clemens and Livy only (accepted by Wren, r4). Sibling echoes moved off: *Overnight*'s "for a long time" (y2, r4), *Still Yours*'s "peel squeezed over the top" (y4 and recipe, r5); closing line clear of the Researcher's "say so". ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/twain-livy-cocktail.md` (F1–F12): Mark Twain Project letter UCCL 01028 (2 January 1874, primary, read on screen); *Oxford Companion* ANGOSTURA BITTERS pdf 112; MTP UCCL 01029 note 3; Paine, *Mark Twain: A Biography* (1912) ch. CIV and CLXXXVIII (secondary). 1874 method: Wondrich, *Imbibe!* pdf 178, 193 (contested; no claim for Twain). Craft: *Cocktail Codex* (Old-Fashioned family); *Flavor Matrix* Grain, pdf 136 (passion fruit, surprise pairing). Room notes: `work/caregiver-lover/`.
names_note: **Standing By**, the room's pick (all three): the letter's own words ("& you standing by"), and it names the person, not the story. Also considered: *The Fourth Thing* (Tomás: the one change, easy to say at a bar), *Four Things Waiting*, *Just How It Sounded*.
open_items: **Unsourced values:** passion fruit syrup (1:1) values are Tomás's, flagged unsourced in Checks.

**Balance caveat (Tomás):** Arnold's stirred acid floor assumes vermouth, so "plain sugar goes OUT on acid" is a range artefact; the claim the room stands on is that 7.5 ml of passion fruit syrup does all the sweetening and adds a sharpness you can hear.
**Closing line alternative:** *Set out everything they asked for. Then add the one thing they didn't, just a little.* (true; recorded for Robin, not a disagreement). The room signed the short form.

**Secondary source:** the swearing story is Clemens's own later telling via Paine: always "the way he told it", no date, no house, never the 1874 bath-room. Livy's reply to the letter isn't on record ("I like to think").

**Not his:** the 1874 method is contested (Thomas shook, the 1869 *Steward & Barkeeper's Manual* says never shake); the lemon's use is unstated, so the peel is ours; only "in a wine-glass" is his. Wondrich's sugarless preference is for Twain's *toddy* (pdf 137), not this drink.
**Runner-up and lanes:** the posset (Hester, `historian-candidates.md`). The Hot Toddy was set aside because *Off Duty* (caregiver-hero) already holds it; the registry's family "?" hid it.
